extracted.intended_audience: NIGMS-funded investigators, NIH program staff, research administrators, and policymakers interested in grant funding behavior
extracted.subtask_short: MIRA vs R01 post-award application analysis
extracted.subtask_description: Statistical and descriptive comparison of post-award grant application behavior by investigators supported by NIGMS MIRA awards versus comparable NIGMS R01 awardees, using cohort splits, matched comparators, counts and proportions, and regression models with robustness checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: MIRA award effort and eligibility restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators who receive MIRA support must dedicate 51% of their research effort toward the grant and are ineligible to apply for or receive other NIGMS research support (with some exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This policy constraint defines an important treatment difference between MIRA and R01 awardees and motivates analysis of whether MIRA awardees apply to other ICs more or less often.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator cohorts by award year
rubrics_metrics.description: Split investigators by the year of their MIRA (or comparable R01) grant and analyze cohorts separately (e.g., FY2016 through FY2020).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cohort analysis accounts for differing amounts of time available to submit post-award applications — later cohorts have less follow-up time, which tends to reduce observed post-award application rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator type: Established (EI) vs Early Stage (ESI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare behavior for established investigators (EI) and early stage investigators (ESI) separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ESIs and EIs can have systematically different application behavior; analyses report results for both groups and note that ESIs tend to submit more post-award applications than EIs (p < 0.0001).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparator group construction / matching (for EI)
rubrics_metrics.description: EI comparators were matched according to race/ethnicity, gender, time since acquisition of first R01, and average annual NIGMS funding to create a comparable R01-funded group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matching on these covariates aims to create a fair comparator group to isolate the effect of receiving MIRA rather than underlying demographic or funding-history differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparator group for ESI
rubrics_metrics.description: For the ESI comparator group, all ESI NIGMS R01 awardees were used (no further matching described).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using the full population of ESI R01 awardees serves as the comparator for ESI MIRA recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome metric: proportion of PIs with at least one post-award application to non-NIGMS ICs
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculate the percentage of investigators in each group who submitted at least one research grant application to an Institute or Center other than NIGMS after receiving their MIRA (or comparable R01) award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses and Figure 1 plot these proportions by cohort and investigator type; the proportion generally declines for later cohorts due to shorter follow-up time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Included grant/application types
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on research project grants (RPGs) and research center grants (type 1 and 2 applications), the two largest categories of NIGMS research grant types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because MIRA awardees cannot apply for additional NIGMS research grants, analysis restricts to applications to other ICs and to these major grant categories to make fair comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome metric: number (count) of post-award non-NIGMS applications per PI
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare the number of post-award applications to ICs other than NIGMS for each PI by cohort, using distributions and summary statistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure 2 uses box plots to show medians, 25th/75th percentiles, and whiskers; differences persist even when excluding PIs with zero post-award applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visualization summary statistics (box plot interpretation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use box plots where the horizontal line is the median, the top and bottom of the box are the 75th and 25th percentiles, and whiskers extend beyond to show values outside the interquartile range.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Box plots summarize the distribution of post-award application counts across groups and cohorts; they visually convey central tendency and variability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regression modeling of post-award application counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform regression analysis modeling the count of post-award applications to other ICs to control for potentially influential variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regression allows testing whether differences between MIRA and comparator PIs remain after adjusting for covariates; reported result: MIRA PIs are associated with fewer post-award applications (p = 0.0001).

rubrics_metrics.name: Covariates controlled in regression
rubrics_metrics.description: Control for variables such as the proportion of a PI’s prior applications going to non-NIGMS ICs and the size of the NIGMS MIRA or comparable R01 grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These covariates capture prior propensity to apply elsewhere and resource level, both of which significantly predict post-award application behavior (prior proportion p < 0.0001; grant size p = 0.001).

rubrics_metrics.name: Key predictors identified
rubrics_metrics.description: Findings identify that the strongest predictor of post-award applications is the proportion of a PI’s prior applications that went to non-NIGMS ICs; grant size is also positively correlated, driven by awards in the $500,000–$750,000 range.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This suggests past application behavior is highly predictive of future patterns, and mid-sized awards may enable additional submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical significance reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Use p-values to assess significance of differences and predictors (examples: p = 0.0001 for MIRA versus comparator difference; p < 0.0001 for ESI vs EI; p = 0.001 for grant size effect).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit p-value reporting is used to support claims of statistically significant differences; no specific alpha threshold is stated but conventional interpretation is implied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robustness checks / alternative model specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify findings are robust to alternative model specifications and model types, such as difference-in-difference and logistic regression models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Robustness checks increase confidence that the observed association (MIRA PIs submit fewer non-NIGMS applications) is not an artifact of one modeling choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time window of data
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyses reflect fiscal years 2016 up to the end of FY 2021.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifying the timeframe is important for interpreting cohort effects and the available follow-up period for post-award submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretive policy criterion: alignment with MIRA program goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether observed behavior aligns with program goals — specifically, MIRA aims to reduce time spent writing grant applications so awardees can focus on research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observed fewer post-award applications by MIRA PIs is interpreted as consistent with the program’s objective to reduce application burden.
